markTaskDone: hands the status change to the domain via task.markDone() instead of setting the status itself.
listTasks: turns the input into domain TaskFilters through TaskStatus.create(...).value and asks the TaskRepository port for the tasks.
The constructor takes the UserRepository, ProjectRepository and TaskRepository interfaces, so no concrete persistence code is in the file.

parsedVerdict.reasoning: TaskService does what an application service should do. Each method gets data through repository ports declared in the domain, builds domain objects, hands state changes to the domain (task.markDone(), TaskStatus.create/todo), saves through the ports and maps the results to DTOs. It does no persistence work itself (no SQL, ORM or storage details), has no transport or framework code (no HTTP request/response handling, status codes or routing), and contains no real business rules. Checking that referenced entities exist (requireProject, the assignee lookup) is ordinary application-level coordination. Turning the dueDate string into a Date is a small DTO-to-domain conversion, which fits at the application boundary.
